name: My last cabinet refacing job peeled and looked uneven—how do I avoid repeating that?

mainEntity.name: My last cabinet refacing job peeled and looked uneven—how do I avoid repeating that?

acceptedAnswer.text:
Cabinet refacing can still be considered after a poor prior experience, but the new project should begin with a condition review and a precise scope. The cause of the earlier failure—bad preparation, moisture, poor measurements, unsuitable materials, or weak installation—must be identified first.

Context: Covering a failed finish without correcting the substrate can repeat the problem. A new provider should be willing to explain what will be removed, repaired, tested, and warrantied.

Key factors:
- Bubbling, peeling, lifting edges, uneven reveals, or loose hardware.
- Moisture sources and damaged cabinet materials.
- Compatibility of the proposed surface with the existing substrate.

Practical guidance: Gather invoices, product names, photos, and warranty documents from the earlier job. Ask for a sample installation or preparation description and require change approvals in writing.

Elite Remodeling & Design can evaluate whether the existing cabinets need repair, partial replacement, or a broader kitchen remodeling solution before new finishes are selected.
acceptedAnswer.description: Find the cause before starting again: moisture, poor preparation, unsuitable materials, inaccurate measurements, or weak installation. Provide prior photos and product information, request a box-condition assessment, review preparation steps, and get the repair and warranty scope in writing.
